title: Why he recorded little and Fazola in his ten-piece band
summary: DeDroit says he recorded only with the Okeh outfit, felt big-band competition made recording pointless, and praises Fazola.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: So you had a ten piece orchestra that you were calling your recording orchestra, besides your...

I only recorded with the Ditchellander. I see. Yeah. I never did attempt to... So the ten piece was your... Because of the changeover with the big bands, I didn't feel that I could do myself any good recording, because there was too many great bands, you know what I mean? To compete, yeah. Yeah. Not in New Orleans, no...

But you had your ten piece band, it was more or less your society orchestra, you would call it... Well I played arrangements. I played arrangements. Then it's arrangements. Yes. And that was at the same...

And it picked up stocks. Yeah. And that was still during the twenties. It was a higher type of a milious set, but I had Fazola on the clarinet, he was great. You know heard of him? His name was... You know heard of Fazola? Yeah, I knew him. His name was Verstappen. That's his real name. That would be hard enough to pronounce. Oh, the greatest clarinet player of the lick. And people don't know it, he played a tenor saxophone. I used to play Spanish tunes, just to hear that guy play lead on it. Oh, he used to send me. You don't know if the band didn't know it, I was getting my kicks as much as the people listen to me. Mm-hm. Mm-hm.
